query.description:
Filters the fields returned in the response

Example:
- `field[]=id`: Return the `id` field
- `field[]=address.id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` object
- `field[]=addresses[].id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` objects

On endpoints that implement the `embed` query parameter, if you specified embeds in your call, you will need to request the `_embed` field as well.
Example:
- `field[]=_embed`: Return all fields from all requested embeds
- `field[]=_embed.address`: Return all fields from the `address` embed
- `field[]=_embed.company.name`: Return the `name` field from the `company` embed

Additional object included in the result.

Each embed object may require different oauth2 scopes than the main endpoint:
- company: `companies.read`
- individual: `individuals.read`
- owner: `staffs.read`
- contact: `contacts.read`
- related: by object type. Check the entire documentation to verify the usual scopes requested for the types returned

Each embed object may require different oauth2 scopes than the main endpoint:
- opportunities: `opportunities.read`

- estimates,invoices,orders,deliveries: `invoicing.read`
- cf.{custom_field_id} : `custom-fields.read`
- smart_tags: `smart-tags.read`
Additionally, the smart_tags embed is limited to the 20 first results sorted in alphabetical order.

Filters the fields returned in the response

Example:
- `field[]=id`: Return the `id` field
- `field[]=address.id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` object
- `field[]=addresses[].id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` objects

On endpoints that implement the `embed` query parameter, if you specified embeds in your call, you will need to request the `_embed` field as well.
Example:
- `field[]=_embed`: Return all fields from all requested embeds
- `field[]=_embed.address`: Return all fields from the `address` embed
- `field[]=_embed.company.name`: Return the `name` field from the `company` embed
Flag to trigger validation only (set to true to validate payload without persisting data)

description.content: Get a list of companies

query.description:
Example : `embed[]=invoicing_contact&embed[]=cf.1542&embed[]=acl`
Additional object included in the result.

Each embed object may require different oauth2 scopes than the main endpoint:
- opportunities: `opportunities.read`
- main_contact, dunning_contact, invoicing_contact: `contacts.read`
- estimates,invoices,orders,deliveries: `invoicing.read`
- cf.{custom_field_id} : `custom-fields.read`
- smart_tags: `smart-tags.read`
Additionally, the smart_tags embed is limited to the 20 first results sorted in alphabetical order.

Filters the fields returned in the response

Example:
- `field[]=id`: Return the `id` field
- `field[]=address.id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` object
- `field[]=addresses[].id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` objects

On endpoints that implement the `embed` query parameter, if you specified embeds in your call, you will need to request the `_embed` field as well.
Example:
- `field[]=_embed`: Return all fields from all requested embeds
- `field[]=_embed.address`: Return all fields from the `address` embed
- `field[]=_embed.company.name`: Return the `name` field from the `company` embed

description.content: Search companies

query.description:
Example : `embed[]=invoicing_contact&embed[]=cf.1542&embed[]=acl`
Additional object included in the result.

Each embed object may require different oauth2 scopes than the main endpoint:
- opportunities: `opportunities.read`
- main_contact, dunning_contact, invoicing_contact: `contacts.read`
- estimates,invoices,orders,deliveries: `invoicing.read`
- cf.{custom_field_id} : `custom-fields.read`
- smart_tags: `smart-tags.read`
Additionally, the smart_tags embed is limited to the 20 first results sorted in alphabetical order.

Filters the fields returned in the response

Example:
- `field[]=id`: Return the `id` field
- `field[]=address.id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` object
- `field[]=addresses[].id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` objects

On endpoints that implement the `embed` query parameter, if you specified embeds in your call, you will need to request the `_embed` field as well.
Example:
- `field[]=_embed`: Return all fields from all requested embeds
- `field[]=_embed.address`: Return all fields from the `address` embed
- `field[]=_embed.company.name`: Return the `name` field from the `company` embed

Each embed object may require different oauth2 scopes than the main endpoint:

Additionally, the smart_tags embed is limited to the 20 first results sorted in alphabetical order.

description.content:
List favourite filters for faster access to specific companies
> Favourite filters can be applied directly to company search endpoints
This route is available in open beta.
Please note that its specifications are potentially subject to significant and breaking changes in the coming weeks.

query.description:
Filters the fields returned in the response

Example:
- `field[]=id`: Return the `id` field
- `field[]=address.id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` object
- `field[]=addresses[].id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` objects

On endpoints that implement the `embed` query parameter, if you specified embeds in your call, you will need to request the `_embed` field as well.
Example:
- `field[]=_embed`: Return all fields from all requested embeds
- `field[]=_embed.address`: Return all fields from the `address` embed
- `field[]=_embed.company.name`: Return the `name` field from the `company` embed

description.content: Update Company informations

query.description:
Example : `embed[]=invoicing_contact&embed[]=cf.1542&embed[]=acl`
Additional object included in the result.

Each embed object may require different oauth2 scopes than the main endpoint:
- opportunities: `opportunities.read`
- main_contact, dunning_contact, invoicing_contact: `contacts.read`
- estimates,invoices,orders,deliveries: `invoicing.read`
- cf.{custom_field_id} : `custom-fields.read`
- smart_tags: `smart-tags.read`
Additionally, the smart_tags embed is limited to the 20 first results sorted in alphabetical order.

Filters the fields returned in the response

Example:
- `field[]=id`: Return the `id` field
- `field[]=address.id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` object
- `field[]=addresses[].id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` objects

On endpoints that implement the `embed` query parameter, if you specified embeds in your call, you will need to request the `_embed` field as well.
Example:
- `field[]=_embed`: Return all fields from all requested embeds
- `field[]=_embed.address`: Return all fields from the `address` embed
- `field[]=_embed.company.name`: Return the `name` field from the `company` embed
Flag to trigger validation only (set to true to validate payload without persisting data)

query.description:
Example : `embed[]=delivery_address&embed[]=cf.1542&embed[]=acl`
Additional object included in the result.

Each embed object may require different oauth2 scopes than the main endpoint:
- opportunities: `opportunities.read`
- estimates,invoices,orders,deliveries: `invoicing.read`
- cf.{custom_field_id} : `custom-fields.read`
- smart_tags: `smart-tags.read`
Additionally, the smart_tags embed is limited to the 20 first results sorted in alphabetical order.

Filters the fields returned in the response

Example:
- `field[]=id`: Return the `id` field
- `field[]=address.id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` object
- `field[]=addresses[].id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` objects

On endpoints that implement the `embed` query parameter, if you specified embeds in your call, you will need to request the `_embed` field as well.
Example:
- `field[]=_embed`: Return all fields from all requested embeds
- `field[]=_embed.address`: Return all fields from the `address` embed
- `field[]=_embed.company.name`: Return the `name` field from the `company` embed

description.content: Get list of custom fields for a company

query.description:
Filters the fields returned in the response

Example:
- `field[]=id`: Return the `id` field
- `field[]=address.id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` object
- `field[]=addresses[].id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` objects

On endpoints that implement the `embed` query parameter, if you specified embeds in your call, you will need to request the `_embed` field as well.
Example:
- `field[]=_embed`: Return all fields from all requested embeds
- `field[]=_embed.address`: Return all fields from the `address` embed
- `field[]=_embed.company.name`: Return the `name` field from the `company` embed

Additional object included in the result.

Each embed object may require different oauth2 scopes than the main endpoint.
value_details will add extra data for custom field of the following types:
- Client/Prospect/Supplier (scope `companies.read`, `individuals.read`)
- Contact (scope `contacts.read`)
- Staff member (scope `staffs.read`)
- Products/services (scope `items.read`)

query.description:
Example : `embed[]=delivery_address&embed[]=cf.1542&embed[]=acl`
Additional object included in the result.

Each embed object may require different oauth2 scopes than the main endpoint:
- opportunities: `opportunities.read`
- estimates,invoices,orders,deliveries: `invoicing.read`
- cf.{custom_field_id} : `custom-fields.read`
- smart_tags: `smart-tags.read`
Additionally, the smart_tags embed is limited to the 20 first results sorted in alphabetical order.

Filters the fields returned in the response

Example:
- `field[]=id`: Return the `id` field
- `field[]=address.id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` object
- `field[]=addresses[].id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` objects

On endpoints that implement the `embed` query parameter, if you specified embeds in your call, you will need to request the `_embed` field as well.
Example:
- `field[]=_embed`: Return all fields from all requested embeds
- `field[]=_embed.address`: Return all fields from the `address` embed
- `field[]=_embed.company.name`: Return the `name` field from the `company` embed

Get the companies of a contact

query.description:
Example : `embed[]=invoicing_contact&embed[]=cf.1542&embed[]=acl`
Additional object included in the result.

Each embed object may require different oauth2 scopes than the main endpoint:
- opportunities: `opportunities.read`
- main_contact, dunning_contact, invoicing_contact: `contacts.read`
- estimates,invoices,orders,deliveries: `invoicing.read`
- cf.{custom_field_id} : `custom-fields.read`
- smart_tags: `smart-tags.read`
Additionally, the smart_tags embed is limited to the 20 first results sorted in alphabetical order.

Example:
- `field[]=id`: Return the `id` field
- `field[]=address.id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` object

On endpoints that implement the `embed` query parameter, if you specified embeds in your call, you will need to request the `_embed` field as well.

- `field[]=_embed`: Return all fields from all requested embeds

Example : `embed[]=payment_method_ids&embed[]=cf.1542&embed[]=acl`
Additional object included in the result.

Each embed object may require different oauth2 scopes than the main endpoint:
- payment_method_ids: `payments.read`
- company: `companies.read`
- individual: `individuals.read`
- contact: `contacts.read`
- cf.{custom_field_id} : `custom-fields.read`
- smart_tags: `smart-tags.read`
Additionally, the smart_tags embed is limited to the 20 first results sorted in alphabetical order.
- related: by object type. Check the entire documentation to verify the usual scopes requested for the types returned

Aggregations on amounts only works in addition with the currency filter

Create an estimate
This route is available in open beta.
Please note that its specifications are potentially subject to significant and breaking changes in the coming weeks.

Electronic invoicing reform

  • The field rows[x].description will become required in a future update. (Description and trade name in sales documents)
  • The field rows[x].tax_id no longer accepts non-compliant taxes. (Managing VAT for electronic invoicing)

query.description:
Filters the fields returned in the response

Example:
- `field[]=id`: Return the `id` field
- `field[]=address.id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` object
- `field[]=addresses[].id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` objects

On endpoints that implement the `embed` query parameter, if you specified embeds in your call, you will need to request the `_embed` field as well.
Example:
- `field[]=_embed`: Return all fields from all requested embeds
- `field[]=_embed.address`: Return all fields from the `address` embed
- `field[]=_embed.company.name`: Return the `name` field from the `company` embed

Example : `embed[]=payment_method_ids&embed[]=cf.1542&embed[]=acl`
Additional object included in the result.

Each embed object may require different oauth2 scopes than the main endpoint:
- payment_method_ids: `payments.read`
- company: `companies.read`
- individual: `individuals.read`
- contact: `contacts.read`
- cf.{custom_field_id} : `custom-fields.read`
- smart_tags: `smart-tags.read`
Additionally, the smart_tags embed is limited to the 20 first results sorted in alphabetical order.
- related: by object type. Check the entire documentation to verify the usual scopes requested for the types returned

Aggregations on amounts only works in addition with the currency filter

The order field
> Value `numero` is deprecated and will be deleted on the July 1st 2022. Use `number` instead.

query.description:
Filters the fields returned in the response

Example:
- `field[]=id`: Return the `id` field
- `field[]=address.id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` object
- `field[]=addresses[].id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` objects

On endpoints that implement the `embed` query parameter, if you specified embeds in your call, you will need to request the `_embed` field as well.
Example:
- `field[]=_embed`: Return all fields from all requested embeds
- `field[]=_embed.address`: Return all fields from the `address` embed
- `field[]=_embed.company.name`: Return the `name` field from the `company` embed

Update an estimate
This route is available in open beta.
Please note that its specifications are potentially subject to significant and breaking changes in the coming weeks.

Electronic invoicing reform

  • The field rows[x].description will become required in a future update. (Description and trade name in sales documents)
  • The field rows[x].tax_id no longer accepts non-compliant taxes. (Managing VAT for electronic invoicing)

query.description:
Example : `embed[]=payment_method_ids&embed[]=cf.1542&embed[]=acl`
Additional object included in the result.

Each embed object may require different oauth2 scopes than the main endpoint:
- payment_method_ids: `payments.read`
- company: `companies.read`
- individual: `individuals.read`
- contact: `contacts.read`
- cf.{custom_field_id} : `custom-fields.read`
- smart_tags: `smart-tags.read`
Additionally, the smart_tags embed is limited to the 20 first results sorted in alphabetical order.
- related: by object type. Check the entire documentation to verify the usual scopes requested for the types returned

Aggregations on amounts only works in addition with the currency filter

Filters the fields returned in the response

Example:
- `field[]=id`: Return the `id` field
- `field[]=address.id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` object
- `field[]=addresses[].id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` objects

On endpoints that implement the `embed` query parameter, if you specified embeds in your call, you will need to request the `_embed` field as well.
Example:
- `field[]=_embed`: Return all fields from all requested embeds
- `field[]=_embed.address`: Return all fields from the `address` embed
- `field[]=_embed.company.name`: Return the `name` field from the `company` embed

query.description:
Filters the fields returned in the response

Example:
- `field[]=id`: Return the `id` field
- `field[]=address.id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` object
- `field[]=addresses[].id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` objects

On endpoints that implement the `embed` query parameter, if you specified embeds in your call, you will need to request the `_embed` field as well.
Example:
- `field[]=_embed`: Return all fields from all requested embeds
- `field[]=_embed.address`: Return all fields from the `address` embed
- `field[]=_embed.company.name`: Return the `name` field from the `company` embed
Additional object included in the result

Create an order
This route is available in open beta.
Please note that its specifications are potentially subject to significant and breaking changes in the coming weeks.

Electronic invoicing reform

  • The field rows[x].description will become required in a future update. (Description and trade name in sales documents)
  • The field rows[x].tax_id no longer accepts non-compliant taxes. (Managing VAT for electronic invoicing)

query.description:
Filters the fields returned in the response

Example:
- `field[]=id`: Return the `id` field
- `field[]=address.id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` object
- `field[]=addresses[].id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` objects

On endpoints that implement the `embed` query parameter, if you specified embeds in your call, you will need to request the `_embed` field as well.
Example:
- `field[]=_embed`: Return all fields from all requested embeds
- `field[]=_embed.address`: Return all fields from the `address` embed
- `field[]=_embed.company.name`: Return the `name` field from the `company` embed

query.description:
Filters the fields returned in the response

Example:
- `field[]=id`: Return the `id` field
- `field[]=address.id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` object
- `field[]=addresses[].id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` objects

On endpoints that implement the `embed` query parameter, if you specified embeds in your call, you will need to request the `_embed` field as well.
Example:
- `field[]=_embed`: Return all fields from all requested embeds
- `field[]=_embed.address`: Return all fields from the `address` embed
- `field[]=_embed.company.name`: Return the `name` field from the `company` embed

Additional object included in the result.

Each embed object may require different oauth2 scopes than the main endpoint.
value_details will add extra data for custom field of the following types:
- Client/Prospect/Supplier (scope `companies.read`, `individuals.read`)
- Contact (scope `contacts.read`)
- Staff member (scope `staffs.read`)
- Products/services (scope `items.read`)

query.description:
Filters the fields returned in the response

Example:
- `field[]=id`: Return the `id` field
- `field[]=address.id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` object
- `field[]=addresses[].id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` objects

On endpoints that implement the `embed` query parameter, if you specified embeds in your call, you will need to request the `_embed` field as well.
Example:
- `field[]=_embed`: Return all fields from all requested embeds
- `field[]=_embed.address`: Return all fields from the `address` embed
- `field[]=_embed.company.name`: Return the `name` field from the `company` embed

query.description:
Filters the fields returned in the response

Example:
- `field[]=id`: Return the `id` field
- `field[]=address.id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` object
- `field[]=addresses[].id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` objects

On endpoints that implement the `embed` query parameter, if you specified embeds in your call, you will need to request the `_embed` field as well.
Example:
- `field[]=_embed`: Return all fields from all requested embeds
- `field[]=_embed.address`: Return all fields from the `address` embed
- `field[]=_embed.company.name`: Return the `name` field from the `company` embed
Additional object included in the result

description.content: Get a list of individuals

query.description:
Example : `embed[]=invoicing_address&embed[]=cf.1542&embed[]=acl`
Additional object included in the result.

Each embed object may require different oauth2 scopes than the main endpoint:
- opportunities: `opportunities.read`
- main_contact, dunning_contact, invoicing_contact: `contacts.read`
- estimates,invoices,orders,deliveries: `invoicing.read`
- cf.{custom_field_id} : `custom-fields.read`
- smart_tags: `smart-tags.read`
Additionally, the smart_tags embed is limited to the 20 first results sorted in alphabetical order.

Filters the fields returned in the response

Example:
- `field[]=id`: Return the `id` field
- `field[]=address.id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` object
- `field[]=addresses[].id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` objects

On endpoints that implement the `embed` query parameter, if you specified embeds in your call, you will need to request the `_embed` field as well.
Example:
- `field[]=_embed`: Return all fields from all requested embeds
- `field[]=_embed.address`: Return all fields from the `address` embed
- `field[]=_embed.company.name`: Return the `name` field from the `company` embed

query.description:
Example : `embed[]=invoicing_address&embed[]=cf.1542&embed[]=acl`
Additional object included in the result.

Each embed object may require different oauth2 scopes than the main endpoint:
- opportunities: `opportunities.read`
- main_contact, dunning_contact, invoicing_contact: `contacts.read`
- estimates,invoices,orders,deliveries: `invoicing.read`
- cf.{custom_field_id} : `custom-fields.read`
- smart_tags: `smart-tags.read`
Additionally, the smart_tags embed is limited to the 20 first results sorted in alphabetical order.

Filters the fields returned in the response

Example:
- `field[]=id`: Return the `id` field
- `field[]=address.id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` object
- `field[]=addresses[].id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` objects

On endpoints that implement the `embed` query parameter, if you specified embeds in your call, you will need to request the `_embed` field as well.
Example:
- `field[]=_embed`: Return all fields from all requested embeds
- `field[]=_embed.address`: Return all fields from the `address` embed
- `field[]=_embed.company.name`: Return the `name` field from the `company` embed
Flag to trigger validation only (set to true to validate payload without persisting data)

query.description:
Example : `embed[]=invoicing_address&embed[]=cf.1542&embed[]=acl`
Additional object included in the result.

Each embed object may require different oauth2 scopes than the main endpoint:
- opportunities: `opportunities.read`
- main_contact, dunning_contact, invoicing_contact: `contacts.read`
- estimates,invoices,orders,deliveries: `invoicing.read`
- cf.{custom_field_id} : `custom-fields.read`
- smart_tags: `smart-tags.read`
Additionally, the smart_tags embed is limited to the 20 first results sorted in alphabetical order.

Filters the fields returned in the response

Example:
- `field[]=id`: Return the `id` field
- `field[]=address.id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` object
- `field[]=addresses[].id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` objects

On endpoints that implement the `embed` query parameter, if you specified embeds in your call, you will need to request the `_embed` field as well.
Example:
- `field[]=_embed`: Return all fields from all requested embeds
- `field[]=_embed.address`: Return all fields from the `address` embed
- `field[]=_embed.company.name`: Return the `name` field from the `company` embed

description.content:
List favourite filters for faster access to specific individuals
> Favourite filters can be applied directly to individual search endpoints
This route is available in open beta.
Please note that its specifications are potentially subject to significant and breaking changes in the coming weeks.

query.description:
Filters the fields returned in the response

Example:
- `field[]=id`: Return the `id` field
- `field[]=address.id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` object
- `field[]=addresses[].id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` objects

On endpoints that implement the `embed` query parameter, if you specified embeds in your call, you will need to request the `_embed` field as well.
Example:
- `field[]=_embed`: Return all fields from all requested embeds
- `field[]=_embed.address`: Return all fields from the `address` embed
- `field[]=_embed.company.name`: Return the `name` field from the `company` embed

response.name: List favourite filters

description.content: Fetch individual informations

query.description:
Example : `embed[]=invoicing_address&embed[]=cf.1542&embed[]=acl`
Additional object included in the result.

Each embed object may require different oauth2 scopes than the main endpoint:
- opportunities: `opportunities.read`
- main_contact, dunning_contact, invoicing_contact: `contacts.read`
- estimates,invoices,orders,deliveries: `invoicing.read`
- cf.{custom_field_id} : `custom-fields.read`
- smart_tags: `smart-tags.read`
Additionally, the smart_tags embed is limited to the 20 first results sorted in alphabetical order.

Filters the fields returned in the response

Example:
- `field[]=id`: Return the `id` field
- `field[]=address.id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` object
- `field[]=addresses[].id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` objects

On endpoints that implement the `embed` query parameter, if you specified embeds in your call, you will need to request the `_embed` field as well.
Example:
- `field[]=_embed`: Return all fields from all requested embeds
- `field[]=_embed.address`: Return all fields from the `address` embed
- `field[]=_embed.company.name`: Return the `name` field from the `company` embed

query.description:
Example : `embed[]=invoicing_address&embed[]=cf.1542&embed[]=acl`
Additional object included in the result.

Each embed object may require different oauth2 scopes than the main endpoint:
- opportunities: `opportunities.read`
- main_contact, dunning_contact, invoicing_contact: `contacts.read`
- estimates,invoices,orders,deliveries: `invoicing.read`
- cf.{custom_field_id} : `custom-fields.read`
- smart_tags: `smart-tags.read`
Additionally, the smart_tags embed is limited to the 20 first results sorted in alphabetical order.

Filters the fields returned in the response

Example:
- `field[]=id`: Return the `id` field
- `field[]=address.id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` object
- `field[]=addresses[].id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` objects

On endpoints that implement the `embed` query parameter, if you specified embeds in your call, you will need to request the `_embed` field as well.
Example:
- `field[]=_embed`: Return all fields from all requested embeds
- `field[]=_embed.address`: Return all fields from the `address` embed
- `field[]=_embed.company.name`: Return the `name` field from the `company` embed
Flag to trigger validation only (set to true to validate payload without persisting data)

- `field[]=_embed`: Return all fields from all requested embeds

query.description:
Example : `embed[]=assigned_staffs&embed[]=cf.1542&embed[]=acl`
Additional object included in the result.

Each embed object may require different oauth2 scopes than the main endpoint:
- company: `companies.read`
- individual: `individuals.read`
- assigned_staffs: `staffs.read`
- contacts: `contacts.read`
- estimates, invoices, orders, deliveries, proformas, creditnotes: `invoicing.read`
- cf.{custom_field_id} : `custom-fields.read`
- smart_tags: `smart-tags.read`
Additionally, the smart_tags embed is limited to the 20 first results sorted in alphabetical order.

Filters the fields returned in the response

Example:
- `field[]=id`: Return the `id` field
- `field[]=address.id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` object
- `field[]=addresses[].id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` objects

On endpoints that implement the `embed` query parameter, if you specified embeds in your call, you will need to request the `_embed` field as well.
Example:
- `field[]=_embed`: Return all fields from all requested embeds
- `field[]=_embed.address`: Return all fields from the `address` embed
- `field[]=_embed.company.name`: Return the `name` field from the `company` embed
Flag to trigger validation only (set to true to validate payload without persisting data)

description.content: Get list of opportunities

query.description:
Additional object included in the result.

Each embed object may require different oauth2 scopes than the main endpoint:
- company: `companies.read`
- individual: `individuals.read`
- assigned_staffs: `staffs.read`
- contacts: `contacts.read`
- estimates, invoices, orders, deliveries, proformas, creditnotes: `invoicing.read`
- cf.{custom_field_id} : `custom-fields.read`
- smart_tags: `smart-tags.read`
Additionally, the smart_tags embed is limited to the 20 first results sorted in alphabetical order.

Filters the fields returned in the response

Example:
- `field[]=id`: Return the `id` field
- `field[]=address.id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` object
- `field[]=addresses[].id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` objects

On endpoints that implement the `embed` query parameter, if you specified embeds in your call, you will need to request the `_embed` field as well.
Example:
- `field[]=_embed`: Return all fields from all requested embeds
- `field[]=_embed.address`: Return all fields from the `address` embed
- `field[]=_embed.company.name`: Return the `name` field from the `company` embed

description.content: Get an opportunity

query.description:
Example : `embed[]=assigned_staffs&embed[]=cf.1542&embed[]=acl`
Additional object included in the result.

Each embed object may require different oauth2 scopes than the main endpoint:
- company: `companies.read`
- individual: `individuals.read`
- assigned_staffs: `staffs.read`
- contacts: `contacts.read`
- estimates, invoices, orders, deliveries, proformas, creditnotes: `invoicing.read`
- cf.{custom_field_id} : `custom-fields.read`
- smart_tags: `smart-tags.read`
Additionally, the smart_tags embed is limited to the 20 first results sorted in alphabetical order.

Filters the fields returned in the response

Example:
- `field[]=id`: Return the `id` field
- `field[]=address.id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` object
- `field[]=addresses[].id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` objects

On endpoints that implement the `embed` query parameter, if you specified embeds in your call, you will need to request the `_embed` field as well.
Example:
- `field[]=_embed`: Return all fields from all requested embeds
- `field[]=_embed.address`: Return all fields from the `address` embed
- `field[]=_embed.company.name`: Return the `name` field from the `company` embed

description.content: Update Opportunity informations

query.description:
Example : `embed[]=assigned_staffs&embed[]=cf.1542&embed[]=acl`
Additional object included in the result.

Each embed object may require different oauth2 scopes than the main endpoint:
- company: `companies.read`
- individual: `individuals.read`
- assigned_staffs: `staffs.read`
- contacts: `contacts.read`
- estimates, invoices, orders, deliveries, proformas, creditnotes: `invoicing.read`
- cf.{custom_field_id} : `custom-fields.read`
- smart_tags: `smart-tags.read`
Additionally, the smart_tags embed is limited to the 20 first results sorted in alphabetical order.

Filters the fields returned in the response

Example:
- `field[]=id`: Return the `id` field
- `field[]=address.id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` object
- `field[]=addresses[].id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` objects

On endpoints that implement the `embed` query parameter, if you specified embeds in your call, you will need to request the `_embed` field as well.
Example:
- `field[]=_embed`: Return all fields from all requested embeds
- `field[]=_embed.address`: Return all fields from the `address` embed
- `field[]=_embed.company.name`: Return the `name` field from the `company` embed
Flag to trigger validation only (set to true to validate payload without persisting data)

description.content:
Partially update an Opportunity on specific properties.
Complex relationships (related, source, contacts, staffs, etc.) are not supported in PATCH.
All fields are optional - only provided fields will be validated and updated.

query.description:
**Required.** List of properties to update.
Only the listed properties will be processed, others will be ignored.
Must use the bracketed array syntax, e.g. `only[]=status&only[]=amount`.

Example : `embed[]=assigned_staffs&embed[]=cf.1542&embed[]=acl`
Additional object included in the result.

Each embed object may require different oauth2 scopes than the main endpoint:
- company: `companies.read`
- individual: `individuals.read`
- assigned_staffs: `staffs.read`
- contacts: `contacts.read`
- estimates, invoices, orders, deliveries, proformas, creditnotes: `invoicing.read`
- cf.{custom_field_id} : `custom-fields.read`
- smart_tags: `smart-tags.read`
Additionally, the smart_tags embed is limited to the 20 first results sorted in alphabetical order.

Filters the fields returned in the response

Example:
- `field[]=id`: Return the `id` field
- `field[]=address.id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` object
- `field[]=addresses[].id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` objects

On endpoints that implement the `embed` query parameter, if you specified embeds in your call, you will need to request the `_embed` field as well.
Example:
- `field[]=_embed`: Return all fields from all requested embeds
- `field[]=_embed.address`: Return all fields from the `address` embed
- `field[]=_embed.company.name`: Return the `name` field from the `company` embed
Flag to trigger validation only (set to true to validate payload without persisting data)

List directories and files attached to an opportunity
This route is available in open beta.
Please note that its specifications are potentially subject to significant and breaking changes in the coming weeks.

description.content: Search opportunities

query.description:
Additional object included in the result.

Each embed object may require different oauth2 scopes than the main endpoint:
- company: `companies.read`
- individual: `individuals.read`
- assigned_staffs: `staffs.read`
- contacts: `contacts.read`
- estimates, invoices, orders, deliveries, proformas, creditnotes: `invoicing.read`
- cf.{custom_field_id} : `custom-fields.read`
- smart_tags: `smart-tags.read`
Additionally, the smart_tags embed is limited to the 20 first results sorted in alphabetical order.

Filters the fields returned in the response

Example:
- `field[]=id`: Return the `id` field
- `field[]=address.id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` object
- `field[]=addresses[].id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` objects

On endpoints that implement the `embed` query parameter, if you specified embeds in your call, you will need to request the `_embed` field as well.
Example:
- `field[]=_embed`: Return all fields from all requested embeds
- `field[]=_embed.address`: Return all fields from the `address` embed
- `field[]=_embed.company.name`: Return the `name` field from the `company` embed

description.content:
List favourite filters for faster access to specific opportunities
> Favourite filters can be applied directly to opportunity search endpoints
This route is available in open beta.
Please note that its specifications are potentially subject to significant and breaking changes in the coming weeks.

query.description:
Filters the fields returned in the response

Example:
- `field[]=id`: Return the `id` field
- `field[]=address.id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` object
- `field[]=addresses[].id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` objects

On endpoints that implement the `embed` query parameter, if you specified embeds in your call, you will need to request the `_embed` field as well.
Example:
- `field[]=_embed`: Return all fields from all requested embeds
- `field[]=_embed.address`: Return all fields from the `address` embed
- `field[]=_embed.company.name`: Return the `name` field from the `company` embed

description.content: Get a list of tasks

query.description:
Additional object included in the result.

Each embed object may require different oauth2 scopes than the main endpoint:
- company: `companies.read`
- individual: `individuals.read`
- owner, assigned_staffs: `staffs.read`
- contact: `contacts.read`
- related: by object type. Check the entire documentation to verify the usual scopes requested for the types returned

Filters the fields returned in the response

Example:
- `field[]=id`: Return the `id` field
- `field[]=address.id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` object
- `field[]=addresses[].id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` objects

On endpoints that implement the `embed` query parameter, if you specified embeds in your call, you will need to request the `_embed` field as well.
Example:
- `field[]=_embed`: Return all fields from all requested embeds
- `field[]=_embed.address`: Return all fields from the `address` embed
- `field[]=_embed.company.name`: Return the `name` field from the `company` embed

query.description:
Filters the fields returned in the response

Example:
- `field[]=id`: Return the `id` field
- `field[]=address.id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` object
- `field[]=addresses[].id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` objects

On endpoints that implement the `embed` query parameter, if you specified embeds in your call, you will need to request the `_embed` field as well.
Example:
- `field[]=_embed`: Return all fields from all requested embeds
- `field[]=_embed.address`: Return all fields from the `address` embed
- `field[]=_embed.company.name`: Return the `name` field from the `company` embed

Additional object included in the result.

Each embed object may require different oauth2 scopes than the main endpoint:
- company: `companies.read`
- individual: `individuals.read`
- owner, assigned_staffs: `staffs.read`
- contact: `contacts.read`
- related: by object type. Check the entire documentation to verify the usual scopes requested for the types returned

description.content: Search tasks

query.description:
Additional object included in the result.

Each embed object may require different oauth2 scopes than the main endpoint:
- company: `companies.read`
- individual: `individuals.read`
- owner, assigned_staffs: `staffs.read`
- contact: `contacts.read`
- related: by object type. Check the entire documentation to verify the usual scopes requested for the types returned

Filters the fields returned in the response

Example:
- `field[]=id`: Return the `id` field
- `field[]=address.id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` object
- `field[]=addresses[].id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` objects

On endpoints that implement the `embed` query parameter, if you specified embeds in your call, you will need to request the `_embed` field as well.
Example:
- `field[]=_embed`: Return all fields from all requested embeds
- `field[]=_embed.address`: Return all fields from the `address` embed
- `field[]=_embed.company.name`: Return the `name` field from the `company` embed

query.description:
Additional object included in the result.

Each embed object may require different oauth2 scopes than the main endpoint:
- company: `companies.read`
- individual: `individuals.read`
- owner: `staffs.read`
- contact: `contacts.read`
- related, participants: by object type. Check the entire documentation to verify the usual scopes requested for the types returned

Filters the fields returned in the response

Example:
- `field[]=id`: Return the `id` field
- `field[]=address.id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` object
- `field[]=addresses[].id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` objects

On endpoints that implement the `embed` query parameter, if you specified embeds in your call, you will need to request the `_embed` field as well.
Example:
- `field[]=_embed`: Return all fields from all requested embeds
- `field[]=_embed.address`: Return all fields from the `address` embed
- `field[]=_embed.company.name`: Return the `name` field from the `company` embed

description.content: Get a list of phoneCalls

query.description:
Filters the fields returned in the response

Example:
- `field[]=id`: Return the `id` field
- `field[]=address.id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` object
- `field[]=addresses[].id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` objects

On endpoints that implement the `embed` query parameter, if you specified embeds in your call, you will need to request the `_embed` field as well.
Example:
- `field[]=_embed`: Return all fields from all requested embeds
- `field[]=_embed.address`: Return all fields from the `address` embed
- `field[]=_embed.company.name`: Return the `name` field from the `company` embed

Additional object included in the result.

Each embed object may require different oauth2 scopes than the main endpoint:
- company: `companies.read`
- individual: `individuals.read`
- owner: `staffs.read`
- contact: `contacts.read`
- related: by object type. Check the entire documentation to verify the usual scopes requested for the types returned

query.description:
Filters the fields returned in the response

Example:
- `field[]=id`: Return the `id` field
- `field[]=address.id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` object
- `field[]=addresses[].id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` objects

On endpoints that implement the `embed` query parameter, if you specified embeds in your call, you will need to request the `_embed` field as well.
Example:
- `field[]=_embed`: Return all fields from all requested embeds
- `field[]=_embed.address`: Return all fields from the `address` embed
- `field[]=_embed.company.name`: Return the `name` field from the `company` embed

Additional object included in the result.

Each embed object may require different oauth2 scopes than the main endpoint:
- company: `companies.read`
- individual: `individuals.read`
- owner: `staffs.read`
- contact: `contacts.read`
- related: by object type. Check the entire documentation to verify the usual scopes requested for the types returned

request.name: Get system email template with content

description.content:
Retrieve the related email template for a context identified by a string. Either the default one, or the content overloaded by the client

| Context                       | Description                                       | Informations                                                         |
| ---                           | ---                                               | ---                                                                  |

query.description: Additional object included in the result

Example:

description.content:
Get list of credit notes linked to an invoice
This route is available in open beta.
Please note that its specifications are potentially subject to significant and breaking changes in the coming weeks.

query.description:
Filters the fields returned in the response

Example:
- `field[]=id`: Return the `id` field
- `field[]=address.id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` object
- `field[]=addresses[].id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` objects

On endpoints that implement the `embed` query parameter, if you specified embeds in your call, you will need to request the `_embed` field as well.
Example:
- `field[]=_embed`: Return all fields from all requested embeds
- `field[]=_embed.address`: Return all fields from the `address` embed
- `field[]=_embed.company.name`: Return the `name` field from the `company` embed

query.description:
Filters the fields returned in the response

Example:
- `field[]=id`: Return the `id` field
- `field[]=address.id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` object
- `field[]=addresses[].id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` objects

On endpoints that implement the `embed` query parameter, if you specified embeds in your call, you will need to request the `_embed` field as well.
Example:
- `field[]=_embed`: Return all fields from all requested embeds
- `field[]=_embed.address`: Return all fields from the `address` embed
- `field[]=_embed.company.name`: Return the `name` field from the `company` embed

Additional object included in the result.

Each embed object may require different oauth2 scopes than the main endpoint.
value_details will add extra data for custom field of the following types:
- Client/Prospect/Supplier (scope `companies.read`, `individuals.read`)
- Contact (scope `contacts.read`)
- Staff member (scope `staffs.read`)
- Products/services (scope `items.read`)

query.description:
Filters the fields returned in the response

Example:
- `field[]=id`: Return the `id` field
- `field[]=address.id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` object
- `field[]=addresses[].id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` objects

On endpoints that implement the `embed` query parameter, if you specified embeds in your call, you will need to request the `_embed` field as well.
Example:
- `field[]=_embed`: Return all fields from all requested embeds
- `field[]=_embed.address`: Return all fields from the `address` embed
- `field[]=_embed.company.name`: Return the `name` field from the `company` embed

Please note that its specifications are potentially subject to significant and breaking changes in the coming weeks.

Electronic invoicing reform

  • The field rows[x].description will become required in a future update. (Description and trade name in sales documents)
  • The field rows[x].tax_id no longer accepts non-compliant taxes. (Managing VAT for electronic invoicing)
  • Some settings.pdf_display fields will be forced to true and any provided value will be ignored. (Display preferences and electronic invoicing)

query.description: Additional object included in the result

Filters the fields returned in the response

Example:
- `field[]=id`: Return the `id` field
- `field[]=address.id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` object
- `field[]=addresses[].id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` objects

On endpoints that implement the `embed` query parameter, if you specified embeds in your call, you will need to request the `_embed` field as well.
Example:
- `field[]=_embed`: Return all fields from all requested embeds
- `field[]=_embed.address`: Return all fields from the `address` embed
- `field[]=_embed.company.name`: Return the `name` field from the `company` embed

query.description:
Filters the fields returned in the response

Example:
- `field[]=id`: Return the `id` field
- `field[]=address.id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` object
- `field[]=addresses[].id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` objects

On endpoints that implement the `embed` query parameter, if you specified embeds in your call, you will need to request the `_embed` field as well.
Example:
- `field[]=_embed`: Return all fields from all requested embeds
- `field[]=_embed.address`: Return all fields from the `address` embed
- `field[]=_embed.company.name`: Return the `name` field from the `company` embed

Additional object included in the result.

Each embed object may require different oauth2 scopes than the main endpoint.
value_details will add extra data for custom field of the following types:
- Client/Prospect/Supplier (scope `companies.read`, `individuals.read`)
- Contact (scope `contacts.read`)
- Staff member (scope `staffs.read`)
- Products/services (scope `items.read`)

Example:
- `field[]=id`: Return the `id` field
- `field[]=address.id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` object

On endpoints that implement the `embed` query parameter, if you specified embeds in your call, you will need to request the `_embed` field as well.
Example:
- `field[]=_embed`: Return all fields from all requested embeds
- `field[]=_embed.address`: Return all fields from the `address` embed
- `field[]=_embed.company.name`: Return the `name` field from the `company` embed

List favourite filters for faster access to specific credit-notes
> Favourite filters can be applied directly to credit-note search endpoints
This route is available in open beta.
Please note that its specifications are potentially subject to significant and breaking changes in the coming weeks.

query.description:
Filters the fields returned in the response

Example:
- `field[]=id`: Return the `id` field
- `field[]=address.id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` object
- `field[]=addresses[].id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` objects

On endpoints that implement the `embed` query parameter, if you specified embeds in your call, you will need to request the `_embed` field as well.
Example:
- `field[]=_embed`: Return all fields from all requested embeds
- `field[]=_embed.address`: Return all fields from the `address` embed
- `field[]=_embed.company.name`: Return the `name` field from the `company` embed

response.name: List favourite filters

On endpoints that implement the `embed` query parameter, if you specified embeds in your call, you will need to request the `_embed` field as well.

- `field[]=_embed`: Return all fields from all requested embeds
- `field[]=_embed.address`: Return all fields from the `address` embed

query.description:
Filters the fields returned in the response

Example:
- `field[]=id`: Return the `id` field
- `field[]=address.id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` object
- `field[]=addresses[].id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` objects

On endpoints that implement the `embed` query parameter, if you specified embeds in your call, you will need to request the `_embed` field as well.
Example:
- `field[]=_embed`: Return all fields from all requested embeds
- `field[]=_embed.address`: Return all fields from the `address` embed
- `field[]=_embed.company.name`: Return the `name` field from the `company` embed

description.content:
Update a progress invoice.
This route is available in open beta.
Please note that its specifications are potentially subject to significant and breaking changes in the coming weeks.

Electronic invoicing reform

  • The field rows[x].description will become required in a future update. (Description and trade name in sales documents)
  • Some settings.pdf_display fields will be forced to true and any provided value will be ignored. (Display preferences and electronic invoicing)

query.description: Additional object included in the result

Filters the fields returned in the response

Example:
- `field[]=id`: Return the `id` field
- `field[]=address.id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` object
- `field[]=addresses[].id`: Return the `id` field of the `address` objects

On endpoints that implement the `embed` query parameter, if you specified embeds in your call, you will need to request the `_embed` field as well.
Example:
- `field[]=_embed`: Return all fields from all requested embeds
- `field[]=_embed.address`: Return all fields from the `address` embed
- `field[]=_embed.company.name`: Return the `name` field from the `company` embed

description.content:
Find out the [Postman collections](dist/postman/CollectionsApiV2.json) with the required [environment variables](dist/postman/Environment.json) Find out the [Changelog](changelog.html) # Unicity of Identifiers
Since August 22, 2024 and as part of a major architectural change aimed at strengthening data segregation, each Sellsy account is now independent in managing the numbering of its objects (contacts, opportunities, products, documents, etc.). [More information in the FAQ](https://help.sellsy.com/fr/articles/9565757-bonnes-pratiques-api-suite-migration)
# Errors The errors are returned in JSON with the following format: ``` { "error": { "code": HTTP_CODE, "message": "Error message", "context": "Error context code" "details": { "FIELD": "Error message" } } ``` The `details` field can contain an object that details the error. It is used in particular during validation to return the invalid fields | HTTP Code | Description | | ------------- | ------------- | | 400 | Validation and logic errors | | 401 | Authentification errors | | 402 | Quotas limit reached or limit of feature reached on your current plan | | 403 | Insufficient privileges | | 404 | Page not found | | 409 | A request conflicts with the current state of the server | | 413 | Payload is too large | | 429 | Quotas of requests reached (See quotas section) | | 5xx | Server errors | # Versioning This API is versioned, the modifications carried out on this one should not generate regression if you respect the following recommendations: - A new field can be added, your code must authorize this - A new error code can be added, your code must deal with unknown errors - On lists, values can be added - A missing field is not equal to `null` To target a specific **major** version of the API, just precise the number in the url: `{url}/v2/{endpoint}` # Quotas A limit on the number of requests per second, minute, day and/or month is applied to each user account. A 429 error will be sent if at least one of the quotas has reached zero. You can know your remaining quota through the headers of the response: - `X-Quota-Remaining-By-Second` - `X-Quota-Remaining-By-Minute` - `X-Quota-Remaining-By-Day` - `X-Quota-Remaining-By-Month` The quotas are counted on each request, even in the event of an error. On the scripts generating a lot of requests, it is therefore necessary to check these values before returning requests. A new 402 error code has created. This error appears when you try to create ressources like a pipeline or custom fields and the quota limit has been reached. # Pagination on list and search requests On list and search requests, the pagination offset can be typed as either an int or a string, depending on the pagination method used. We provide 2 ways to interact with the pagination. ### 1. "Seek" method The offset value represents the LAST object in the response list, it's the default one used. **We recommend to use the "seek" method, it has better performance and includes optimizations.** ``` GET {{url}}/comments?limit=1 { "data": [ { "id": 1 } ], "pagination": { "limit": 1, "count": 1, "total": 13, "offset": "WyIxMSJd" } } --- GET {{url}}/comments?limit=1&offset=WyIxMSJd { "data": [ { "id": 2 } ], "pagination": { "limit": 1, "count": 1, "total": 13, "offset": "SoIxNyJd" } } ``` ### 2. Numeric offset method The second method, more classical, where the offset corresponds to the number of the result page, it must be explicitly specified in the first request. **We have applied a limit to the first 100 000 results on this method, for performance purposes.** ``` GET {{url}}/comments?limit=1&offset=0 { "data": [ { "id": 1 } ], "pagination": { "limit": 1, "count": 1, "total": 13, "offset": 0 } } --- GET {{url}}/comments?limit=1&offset=1 { "data": [ { "id": 2 } ], "pagination": { "limit": 1, "count": 1, "total": 13, "offset": 1 } } ``` # Embed objects Additional objects can be included in the result, and are specified on each endpoint under the `embed` parameter. Those objects may require different OAuth2 scopes than the main endpoint, and will automatically be `null` if the scopes are not respected. Usually, the scopes are listed in the description of the parameter. Contact Support: Email: api@sellsy.com
